  "text": "The gulls were back by seven. Tobias Reel heard them from the church porch, where he had sat the night out with his cap on his knee, and did not look up at them. He had not slept. He had not prayed either, exactly, though his mouth had moved.\n\nThe tide was where it should be. He checked that first. Then he went down the hill road, because it was the only road, and because a man who does not go back is only a man who has not gone back yet.\n\nThe house stood as it always had. The door was shut. He put his thumb on the latch and it lifted clean.\n\nThe front room was dark. The lamp was on the sill, unlit, the chip in its base turned to the glass. Her father's rug lay square on the dry boards. Nothing was wet. Nothing was out of place, and that was what he kept coming back to afterward, when the Halloran girl asked him and when the minister asked him: nothing had been moved.\n\nHe went out onto the beach. Eleven posts, and the sand around them smooth as a sheet pulled tight. No footprints going down. No footprints coming up.\n\nHe stood a long time with the sea at his boots, flat and ordinary and the colour of pewter, and he did not look into it. That was the whole of what he knew. He had been told, once, by someone who was gone now, that it was the not-looking that mattered.\n\nHe turned, and went up the hill.",
